message.content:
**Sikhae (식해)**  
A chilled Korean “raw‑fish” dish that’s simple to make, great for a light lunch or a side dish at a barbecue.  
It’s essentially a marinated seafood salad—no cooking required, just a good quality, sushi‑grade fish and a flavorful sauce.

---

## Ingredients (for 4 servings)

| Category | Item | Amount |
|----------|------|--------|
| **Seafood** | Fresh sashimi‑grade fish (e.g., tuna, salmon, yellowtail) | 300 g |
| | Shrimp (peeled, deveined) | 100 g |
| | Squid (cleaned, sliced) | 100 g |
| | Optional: clams or mussels (cooked) | 50 g |
| **Vegetables** | Cucumber (julienned) | ½ cup |
| | Red onion (thinly sliced) | ¼ cup |
| | Scallions (chopped) | 2 tbsp |
| | Sesame seeds (toasted) | 1 tsp |
| **Sauce** | Gochujang (Korean red pepper paste) | 2 tbsp |
| | Soy sauce | 1 tbsp |
| | Rice vinegar | 1 tbsp |
| | Sesame oil | 1 tsp |
| | Sugar or honey | ½ tsp |
| | Garlic (minced) | ½ tsp |
| | Chili flakes (optional) | ¼ tsp |
| | Lime or lemon juice | 1 tsp |
| **Optional Garnish** | Fresh cilantro or parsley | 1 tbsp |
| | Thinly sliced chili | 1 tsp |

> **Tip:** Use only sushi‑grade fish or seafood that has been handled properly to avoid food‑borne illness. Keep everything chilled until you’re ready to serve.

---

## Preparation Steps

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | **Prep the seafood** – Slice the fish into thin, bite‑size strips (about ¼‑inch thick). If using shrimp or squid, cut them into small pieces. Keep all seafood on ice. |
| 2 | **Make the sauce** – In a bowl, whisk together gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, minced garlic, chili flakes (if using), and lime/lemon juice until smooth. Taste and adjust: more gochujang for heat, more vinegar for tang, or a touch more sugar for sweetness. |
| 3 | **Marinate** – Toss the sliced fish and seafood in the sauce, making sure every piece is coated. Add the cucumber, onion, scallions, and sesame seeds. Mix gently. |
| 4 | **Chill** – Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 2 hours). The flavors meld and the seafood stays fresh. |
| 5 | **Serve** – Transfer the marinated seafood to a chilled platter or individual bowls. Garnish with fresh cilantro, extra chili flakes, or a drizzle of sesame oil if desired. Serve immediately with a side of steamed rice, kimchi, or a light soup. |

---

## Variations & Tips

| Variation | How to Adapt |
|-----------|--------------|
| **Add more protein** | Include thinly sliced beef or pork (sashimi‑grade) for a richer dish. |
| **Make it spicy** | Increase the amount of gochujang or add a splash of sriracha. |
| **Add crunch** | Toss in thinly sliced radish or carrot for extra texture. |
| **Make it vegan** | Replace seafood with tofu cubes or tempeh, and use a vegan gochujang. |
| **Make it a meal** | Serve with a bowl of hot rice soup (e.g., doenjang jjigae) for a complete Korean meal. |

---

### Quick Reference

| Ingredient | Quantity | Notes |
|------------|----------|-------|
| Fish | 300 g | Sashimi‑grade, thinly sliced |
| Shrimp | 100 g | Peeled, deveined |
| Squid | 100 g | Cleaned, sliced |
| Gochujang | 2 Tbsp | Adjust for heat |
| Soy sauce | 1 Tbsp | |
| Rice vinegar | 1 Tbsp | |
| Sesame oil | 1 tsp | |
| Sugar | ½ tsp | |
| Garlic | ½ tsp | Minced |
| Chili flakes | ¼ tsp | Optional |
| Lime juice | 1 tsp | |
| Cucumber | ½ cup | Julienned |
| Onion | ¼ cup | Thinly sliced |
| Scallions | 2 Tbsp | Chopped |
| Sesame seeds | 1 tsp | Toasted |
| Garnish | 1 Tbsp | Cilantro or parsley |

---

Enjoy your homemade **Sikhae**! It’s a refreshing, savory dish that showcases the delicate flavors of fresh seafood, perfect for a quick, healthy meal or a stylish side at any gathering.
